summary: Trace links missing from usage heatmap after retention compaction for segmented queries
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that several trace links ("trace_id" -> trace view) are not present on console heatmaps or in the segmented usage rollups after nightly retention compaction. The missing links are only for queries that include a segmentation filter (org_id + route) and older than the retention window but still within the expected rollup TTL.

Impact:
- Multiple customers (first reported by NimbleMaps) see dashboards with empty trace-links on heatmap cells for historical data.
- Alert cards that rely on trace linking are firing without being able to attach traces, causing noise in on-call.
- Affects troubleshooting (support and SRE) for production incidents where historical traces are needed.

Environment:
- Production (us-east-1)
- Console version: v2026.02.3
- Retention compaction job: retention-pruner v1.8.2 running nightly 03:30 UTC

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1. Query console heatmap for route: "/api/v1/ingest" with segmentation by org_id for timeframe 2026-02-01 to 2026-02-28.
2. Click some heatmap cells to view attached trace links.
3. Note that ~15-20% of the cells that historically contained trace links now show "No traces available".
4. Run same query for a non-segmented time range -> trace links present as expected.

Observed behavior:
- Traces are present in raw span storage (customer provided S3 snapshot with spans), but console heatmap tile metadata lacks the trace_id references for segmented rollups.
- The usage rollup object for segmented keys shows token counts and p95 latency but has empty "trace_refs" arrays.

Expected behavior:
- Rollups that include trace references to sampled spans should retain a pointer (trace_id) for the top few representative traces even after compaction, so console cells can link back to traces for historical troubleshooting.

Attachments / logs provided by customer:
- Example heatmap screenshot (attached to ticket)
- Redacted span bundle (S3 link) with representative trace ids
- Console query id: q_2026-03-11_9861 (customer saved query)

Additional notes:
- Customer believes the issue began after a retention-pruner configuration change rolled out 2026-03-02 that aggressively removed per-segment metadata earlier than the rollup TTL.
investigation_notes:
Initial triage (03/12): Support confirmed customer query and verified missing trace refs in rollup documents for segmented keys. Indexing and raw spans present in S3.
SRE triage (03/13): Replayed retention-pruner job in staging against a snapshot and observed that when compaction prunes per-segment ephemeral metadata, trace_refs are not migrated into the persistent rollup summary for segments with low sample counts. Potential race between rollup-merge and retention-pruner.
Engineering hypothesis (03/13): Edge case occurs when: 1) a segment receives sparse traffic, 2) rollup flush occurs close to retention cutoff, and 3) retention-pruner marks ephemeral metadata as expired before rollup-merge migrates trace_refs into the persistent bucket. This leaves the persisted rollup without trace pointers.
Evidence: grep of persisted rollup documents shows null/empty trace_refs only for segments whose last-rollup-timestamp is within 2 hours of retention TTL boundary.
timeline:
2026-03-11 - Customer first opened support chat reporting missing trace links.
2026-03-12 - Ticket created; Support gathered query ids and artifacts.
2026-03-13 - SRE reproduced issue in staging with replayed compaction run; hypothesis formed.
2026-03-14 - Engineering started a patch to ensure rollup-merge promotes trace_refs before retention-pruner deletes ephemeral metadata.
workaround:
For impacted customers temporarily: disable aggressive retention-pruner rollout (rollback to pre-2026-03-02 config) or increase segment retention cutoff by 48 hours to avoid race with rollup-merge. Support can also run an on-demand backfill job to repopulate trace_refs for the affected date ranges using raw span snapshots.
Customer-facing workaround shared to NimbleMaps on 2026-03-12: increase query window and remove segmentation filter until backfill completes (reduces granularity but restores trace links).
resolution:
TBD - engineering patch in progress (PR referenced). Targeting forward-fix deployment 2026-03-16 and a one-off backfill job for affected date ranges. Post-deploy we will validate with the customer's sample queries and provide remediation notes.
Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3245 (in review as of 2026-03-14).
